title: Custom ~= Patterns in switch
hints: A `switch` case uses `~=` to decide whether it matches.
Overload `~=` for a `Prefix` struct and for a `(String) -> Bool` closure.
jsBridge: Overloading `~=` teaches `switch` new pattern types, such as prefix structs or predicate closures. That has no JS equivalent, since JS `switch` only uses `===`.

compass.q: How close can JS `switch(true)` get to custom patterns? What's missing?
Which argument of `~=` is the pattern and which is the value? What happens if you swap them?
Custom `~=` vs `case let x where x.hasPrefix(…)`: when is the overload worth it?
Matching HTTP status ranges (`case 200..<300`) uses built-in `~=`. What custom pattern would help your networking code?
